_schema.description: General grammar/revising-editing drill questions sourced from a Kaplan workbook ("The Kaplan Method for Revising/Editing Text", Chapters 3-4), not tied to any specific lettered SHSAT practice exam. No answer key was provided in the source material -- every correct answer and reasoning explanation here was determined by the assistant through direct grammatical/rhetorical analysis, not transcribed from a printed key. Questions with correct=null were genuinely ambiguous or indeterminate on careful analysis and were not force-guessed. Intended as a reference pool for building new custom practice questions and as source material for the Revising & Editing Study Guide.
_schema.source: Kaplan workbook, "The Kaplan Method for Revising/Editing Text" (Chapter 3: Lesson 3.1 Perform Sets 1-2, Revising/Editing Passage-Based Questions; Chapter 4: Revising/Editing Text Skills Review), pages 37-49 and 90-136 approx.
_schema.answer_methodology: No answer key existed for this material. Every question was solved independently via explicit grammar-rule verification (identifying the specific rule violated: subject-verb agreement, dangling/misplaced modifier, comma splice/run-on, vague pronoun reference, parallelism, punctuation rules, etc.), rhetorical analysis (logical relationship between ideas, main topic identification, style/register matching), or process-of-elimination against the other three options. A self-check pass verified no other option was equally defensible before finalizing each answer.
_schema.usage_tracking_note: Questions carry a used_in array once selected into a practice set, so future sets can skip already-used fodder. Check this field before picking new ones.

sentence_construction.question: Read this paragraph. (1) Colleges could give greater support to men's sports teams than to women's teams prior to 1972; today, women's and men's teams must receive equal funding. (2) Title IX of the Education Amendments prohibits gender discrimination at colleges and other federally funded institutions. (3) Resulted in more money in athletic departments allocated for women's sports, greater competition among teams, and improvements in the quality of athletics for women. (4) Title IX has led to more interest in women's sports. Which sentence contains an error in its construction and should be revised?
sentence_construction.reasoning: Sentence 3 is a fragment missing a subject - 'Resulted in...' has no subject performing the action.

sentence_construction.question: Read this sentence. To raise money for uniforms, a car wash will be held by members of the volleyball team on Saturday. How should the sentence be revised?

options.A: Members of the volleyball team, on Saturday to raise money for uniforms, will hold a car wash.
options.B: To raise money for uniforms, on Saturday a car wash will be held by members of the volleyball team.
options.C: On Saturday to raise money for uniforms, members of the volleyball team will hold a car wash.
options.D: To raise money for uniforms, members of the volleyball team will hold a car wash on Saturday.

sentence_construction.reasoning: Dangling modifier: 'to raise money for uniforms' must be followed by the people doing the raising, not 'a car wash'. D cleanly places 'members of the volleyball team' right after the purpose clause, with 'on Saturday' naturally at the end. (A inserts an awkward parenthetical between subject/verb; B still leaves 'a car wash' as what's modified; C stacks two different modifier types awkwardly up front.) Moderate confidence - C is a weaker alternate fix.

sentence_construction.question: Read this paragraph (California condor). (1) Since only 17 of them were living in 1986, the California condor faced extinction, but the population has since flourished and increased to more than 350 in the wild. (2) Despite weighing at least 25 pounds, this vulture can glide as far as 10 miles without ever flapping its wings. (3) It feeds on large carcasses, the bird does not attack any living creatures. (4) To successfully protect them from extinction, concerned groups took the California condors from their mountain habitats and bred them in captivity. Which sentence contains an error in its construction and should be revised?
sentence_construction.reasoning: Sentence 3 is a comma splice: two independent clauses joined only by a comma.

sentence_construction.question: Read this paragraph (Cathedral windows). (1) Cathedral windows are often intricate, composed of thousands of pieces of luminous stained glass. (2) Light changes throughout the day and with the seasons, the windows' brightness can vary as a result. (3) Starting in the twelfth century, European churches installed beautiful stained glass windows. (4) In the nineteenth-century, interest in this glass renewed when artists began to use stained glass in various types of decorative objects. Which sentence contains an error in its construction and should be revised?
sentence_construction.reasoning: Sentence 2 is a comma splice joining two independent clauses with only a comma.

sentence_construction.question: Read this paragraph (William Howard Taft). (1) William Howard Taft served as president of the United States from 1909 to 1913, he was not finished with public service, though, and went on to serve as chief justice of the Supreme Court from 1921 to 1930. (2) Before Taft was elected president, President Theodore Roosevelt had offered him the position of chief justice twice, but he declined the offers due to his commitments as governor of the Philippines. (3) He succeeded Roosevelt as president and is the only person to have served as both president and chief justice. (4) He was the third generation in his family to pursue law, so as chief justice he enjoyed his work tremendously. Which sentence contains an error in its construction and should be revised?
sentence_construction.reasoning: Sentence 1 is a comma splice: '...from 1909 to 1913' + 'he was not finished with public service' are independent clauses joined with just a comma.

sentence_construction.question: Baker California thermometer paragraph. (1) Baker, California... is the site of the world's largest thermometer. (2) Tourists might need the thermometer to remind them that they are driving toward Death Valley, which has record temperatures. (3) This once-thriving mining town was originally known as Berry, named after an old prospector and had a lively community. (4) When the area later underwent development, the town received the name of a railway company's president. Which sentence contains an error in its construction and should be revised?
sentence_construction.reasoning: Sentence 3 lacks a comma after 'prospector', causing 'named after an old prospector and had a lively community' to misleadingly read as one unit attached to 'Berry' rather than 'had' being parallel to 'was known' (town was known... and had...).

sentence_construction.question: Inca/Cuzco paragraph. (1) The Inca viewed the Cuzco Valley's ancient capital, Cuzco, as the center of the world. (2) In fact, it physically linked many cultures of various backgrounds. (3) When civil war weakened the Inca Empire, the Spanish rulers Francisco Pizarro and Diego de Almagro attempted to seize the land. (4) Captured by the Spanish conquistadores in 1503, colonization was a development that left many of the Incas in Cuzco overwhelmed with fear and worry. Which sentence contains an error in its construction and should be revised?
sentence_construction.reasoning: Dangling modifier: 'Captured by the Spanish conquistadores in 1503' must modify a person/place that was captured, but the subject that follows is 'colonization', which cannot itself be captured.

sentence_construction.question: Volcano paragraph (underlined phrases). To protect people living in danger zones, scientists attempt to forecast destructive volcanic eruptions and then send out warnings. Active volcanoes are monitored closely, seismologists observe warning signs, such as swelling caused by magma, to predict when eruptions will occur. They use instruments such as tiltmeters and seismographs to measure and trace ground movement. In addition, scientists can measure gas from surface vents as well as magnetic and electrical properties of the volcano's interior. Which revision corrects the error in sentence structure in the paragraph?
sentence_construction.reasoning: Comma splice: 'Active volcanoes are monitored closely' and 'seismologists observe warning signs...' are both independent clauses joined only by a comma. Changing the comma to a semicolon fixes it.

sentence_construction.question: Dinosaur paragraph (drag format). (1) Paleontologists study dinosaurs by excavating fossils and looking for other signs left behind by the ancient reptiles, which they have classified. (2) Lizard-hipped dinosaurs represent one group and include some carnivores such as Tyrannosaurus. (3) The bird-hipped dinosaur group consists of herbivores such as Stegosaurus. (4) For 125 million years, dinosaurs roamed Earth until they suddenly and mysteriously disappeared. Which sentence in the paragraph contains an error in construction? (drag to box)
sentence_construction.reasoning: The relative clause 'which they have classified' sits immediately after 'the ancient reptiles' but logically should refer to the fossils/signs being classified, not the reptiles themselves as a blanket group - ambiguous modifier attachment. LOW CONFIDENCE - no other sentence has a clearer error, but this one is subtle; flagging as uncertain.

sentence_construction.question: Political advertisement paragraph. (1) The winner of an election is often the candidate who best masters the art of political advertisement. (2) Most voters have a stake in the issues of the day but cannot make sense of the rules and rhetoric of the real processes of government. (3) The 30-second commercial on prime-time television-making sense out of technical political jargon plays a crucial part in the political process. (4) Those who wish to speak for an electorate must make their case to that electorate, and the political advertisement is the most direct and effective way to achieve that goal. Which sentence contains an error in its construction and should be revised?
sentence_construction.reasoning: Sentence 3 opens a parenthetical with a dash ('-making sense out of technical political jargon') but never closes it before 'plays', making it read as though 'jargon' is the subject of 'plays' rather than 'the commercial'.

sentence_construction.question: Liberty Bell paragraph. (1) The Liberty Bell was originally hung in Philadelphia's State House and became associated on many historic events. (2) For example, it rang out during the Boston Tea Party and for the first public reading of the Declaration of Independence. (3) When the British Army prepared to occupy Philadelphia, the Liberty Bell was moved to a church that provided a hiding place. (4) In its current location at Independence Hall, the historic bell draws more than a million visitors each year. Which sentence contains an error in its construction and should be revised?
sentence_construction.reasoning: Sentence 1 uses the wrong preposition: 'became associated on' should be 'became associated with'.

sentence_construction.question: Richard Wright / Black Boy paragraph. (1) Richard Wright's autobiography, Black Boy, discusses his childhood in the Deep South. (2) The grandson of slaves, Wright has lived in Mississippi and Tennessee and then moved to Chicago. (3) There, he signed up for an opportunity to write through the Federal Writer's Project and eventually wrote novels, novellas, and short stories protesting the treatment of African Americans. (4) His book Native Son became a stage play as well as a motion picture in Argentina. Which sentence contains an error in its construction and should be revised?
sentence_construction.reasoning: Sentence 2 mixes verb tenses incorrectly: 'has lived...and then moved' - the present perfect 'has lived' doesn't agree with the simple past sequential action 'then moved'; should be simple past 'lived...and then moved' throughout.

sentence_construction.question: Tolkien / Lord of the Rings paragraph. (1) A winning combination that led to tremendous box office success, the production of the Lord of the Rings trilogy mixed gripping climaxes with interesting details. (2) J. R. R. Tolkien wrote these popular novels, which included elves, dwarves, and other magical characters engaged in thrilling adventures. (3) Sometimes, it took him approximately 10 years to write a book, since Tolkien had high standards for his literature. (4) In addition to making his living as a writer, he was a professor at Oxford University and taught several languages. Which sentence contains an error in its construction and should be revised?
sentence_construction.ambiguous_note: Could not identify a clear construction error among the four sentences on careful re-analysis - all four appear grammatically sound (S1's appositive is valid, S2 is fine, S3's pronoun-before-restated-name is unusual phrasing but not ungrammatical since 'him' already has a clear antecedent from S2, S4 is fine). Flagging as genuinely uncertain rather than forcing a guess.

sentence_construction.question: Beatles paragraph. (1) In the 1960s, Paul McCartney, John Lennon, George Harrison, and Ringo Starr formed the Beatles and soon dominated the music world. (2) Receiving more publicity and more airplay compared with the Rolling Stones, the Beatles were the first British pop group sensation in the United States. (3) With numerous albums, the Beatles maintained superstar status around the world. (4) They remain near the very top of the charts as one of the best-selling musical acts of all time. Which sentence contains an error in its construction and should be revised?
sentence_construction.ambiguous_note: Could not identify a clear grammatical construction error among the four sentences - all four appear structurally sound on careful re-analysis. Flagging as genuinely uncertain rather than forcing a guess.

sentence_construction.question: California air pollution paragraph. (1) The air pollution levels in California could be reduced by implementing better public transit systems, encouraging carpools, and inventing new ways to control exhaust fumes from automobiles. (2) In other parts of the United States, people might not realize that Californians must take their older cars to the shop for regular smog tests. (3) Due to the sprawling population and the lack of a city center, large cities require people to coordinate ways to reach their destinations while still considering their cars' impact on air quality. (4) Despite current challenges and efforts, citizens continue to explore alternative modes of transportation and might decide on drive more environmentally friendly vehicles. Which sentence contains an error in its construction and should be revised?
sentence_construction.reasoning: 'might decide on drive' is ungrammatical - 'decide on' must be followed by a noun/gerund ('decide on driving') or restructured as 'decide to drive', not the bare verb 'drive'.

sentence_construction.question: Sandstone/limestone/shale paragraph. (1) Sandstone, limestone, and shale are three common types of water-made rocks, and it all can play a role in fossil creation. (2) Shale is composed of mud, often containing distinct layers that have dried together, and it is usually formed by erosion from landmasses. (3) By contrast, sandstone is made up of grains of sand that, with the help of water, have adhered to one another over time, frequently trapping and fossilizing simple sea creatures and plants in the process. (4) Sandstone and limestone typically come from the ocean bottom. Which sentence contains an error in its construction and should be revised?
sentence_construction.reasoning: Pronoun-antecedent agreement error: 'Sandstone, limestone, and shale' (three items, plural) is referred to with the singular 'it all' - should be 'they all'.
sentence_construction.confidence: medium - note the paragraph also has an underlying content/logic inconsistency about which rock forms which way across S2-S4, but that is a content issue rather than a construction (grammar) error, so S1's clear pronoun-agreement error is the better fit for this question type.

sentence_construction.question: Lincoln paragraph. (1) Abraham Lincoln distinguished himself as a remarkable orator and was admired more for the Gettysburg Address and his two inaugural speeches. (2) His humble, patient, serious, and persuasive personality helped him gain attention. (3) When Lincoln ran for Senate reelection, he challenged Stephen A. Douglas to a discussion of issues; these became the Lincoln-Douglas debates. (4) Although Lincoln lost that election, he received countless invitations to speak all over the country. Which sentence contains an error in its construction and should be revised?
sentence_construction.reasoning: 'was admired more for X' is a dangling/incomplete comparative - no 'than' comparison point is given and no clear basis for 'more' versus 'most'. Medium confidence - sentences 2-4 are all clean, making S1 the best candidate by elimination.

sentence_construction.question: Competitive sports paragraph. (1) Studies show that people who participate in competitive sports when they are in college tend toward remaining physically active throughout their lives. (2) Research shows that regular physical exercise keeps the brain strong, regardless of one's age. (3) Competitive sports offer additional cognitive challenges, but any type of workout leads to the resilience of the brain later in life. (4) Complex physical activities might require more communication among various parts of the brain, which could lead to brain preservation. Which sentence contains an error in its construction and should be revised?
sentence_construction.ambiguous_note: No sentence has a clear grammatical error on close analysis; S1's 'tend toward remaining' is slightly unusual phrasing but not ungrammatical. Flagging as uncertain rather than forcing a guess.

sentence_construction.question: Data analysis paragraph. (1) Data analysis, statistics, and probability are all included in this year's math class. (2) These are types of applied mathematics, which differ from pure mathematics such as algebra. (3) For example, after completing this class, statistics can be used to improve agriculture and evaluate the results of scientific experiments. (4) Other branches of statistics involve polling, market research, manufacturing, and quality control, just a few of the fields where statistics are used daily. Which sentence contains an error in its construction and should be revised?
sentence_construction.reasoning: Dangling modifier: 'after completing this class' must modify a person (a student), but the subject that follows, 'statistics', cannot itself complete a class.

sentence_construction.question: Northern Lights paragraph. (1) The Northern Lights can awe many local residents, since they rarely appear in southern regions. (2) These shimmering lights occur most often near Earth's north and south magnetic poles. (3) When the mysterious presentations occur far away from the poles, they light up the sky more frequently during periods of solar activity such as sunspots. (4) It is important to note that the Northern Lights can display not only rays of intense colors but also shimmering arcs and bright curtains. Which sentence contains an error in its construction and should be revised?
sentence_construction.reasoning: Sentence 3 reverses the logical cause-effect relationship: solar activity (sunspots) causes the lights to appear farther from the poles, not the reverse as currently phrased ('When...occur far away from the poles, they light up...more frequently during...solar activity').

sentence_construction.question: Baptornis dinosaur paragraph (click-to-select format). Recent fossil evidence suggests that carnivorous dinosaurs were accomplished [swimmers. The] Baptornis looked like a diving bird... It probably had webbed feet and a torpedo-shaped [body, allowing] it to dive. Much like modern penguins and cormorants, which have denser bones than most birds to enable them to stay [submerged. The] Baptornis had a body built for pursuing prey through the water. If this dinosaur was indeed a [swimmer, it] must have used its small, sharp teeth to catch fish in central North America's shallow seas. Which part of the paragraph contains an error in sentence structure?
sentence_construction.reasoning: 'Much like modern penguins and cormorants, which have denser bones than most birds to enable them to stay submerged.' is a sentence fragment (a comparison phrase with no main clause of its own). The period after 'submerged' should be a comma, continuing into 'the Baptornis had a body built...' as the main clause the comparison attaches to.

sentence_construction.question: Learning styles paragraph. (1) According to Howard Gardner, there are people that learn best when they hear information, but most learners benefit from having visual displays. (2) College students have adapted to traditional types of instruction, yet even auditory learners tend to have multiple learning styles. (3) University professors are, therefore, frequently encouraged to utilize multimedia materials in their class presentations. (4) With new advances each day, educational technology offers students and educators a wealth of options. Which sentence contains an error in its construction and should be revised?
sentence_construction.reasoning: 'yet' signals a false contrast - adapting to traditional instruction and having multiple learning styles are compatible facts, not contrasting ones.

sentence_construction.question: Rosalind Franklin paragraph. (1) Rosalind Franklin used the technique of X-ray crystallography to depict the structure of DNA by mapping the basic structure of the tiny molecules. (2) Because she has been celebrated by today's genetic researchers, Franklin was never recognized during her lifetime for her groundbreaking work. (3) Her valuable photos of a hydrated form of DNA greatly helped Watson and Crick portray the full structure of DNA. (4) As a result, these men received the Nobel Prize for their work. Which sentence contains an error in its construction and should be revised?
sentence_construction.reasoning: 'Because X, Y' wrongly implies being celebrated today caused her lack of recognition during her lifetime - these are a contrast, not cause-effect, so 'Because' should be 'Although'.

sentence_construction.question: Australia paragraph (click-to-select format). The island continent of Australia consists of plateaus, ranges, plains, and coasts, which attract tourists and other people seeking adventure. Most Australians live in the warm and sunny coastal cities, including Sydney. Over the years, immigrants have arrived from places such as Europe and the United States for the gold rushes, many other reasons. Which revision corrects the error in sentence structure in the paragraph?
sentence_construction.reasoning: 'for the gold rushes, many other reasons' is an incomplete/unclear construction - inserting 'among' ('for the gold rushes, among many other reasons') fixes it.

sentence_construction.question: Dolores Huerta paragraph. (1) Dolores Huerta, one of the founders of the United Farm Workers union, has been a tireless advocate for California's field workers. (2) The combined efforts of the United Farm Workers union also included the work of Cesar Chavez, who organized the Chicano migrant farmers in California. (3) Both worked hard to help farmworkers. (4) After persevering through confrontations, strikes, and pickets, farmworkers eventually received improved working conditions. Which sentence contains an error in its construction and should be revised?
sentence_construction.reasoning: Dangling modifier: 'After persevering through confrontations, strikes, and pickets' should modify the advocates (Huerta and Chavez) who persevered, not 'farmworkers', who are described as receiving the resulting improved conditions.

sentence_construction.question: Cryptologist paragraph (drag format). (1) As specialists in the technology of deciphering messages, complex mathematical formulas are employed by cryptologists to dissect vital communications. (2) For example, the specialist unlocks codes and ciphers, which are devices that secretly send information. (3) Machines create complex messages consisting of letters, words, numbers, or symbols. (4) During wartime, international groups have attempted to monitor and solve systems since having the opponent's information could provide a major advantage. Which sentence contains an error in construction?
sentence_construction.reasoning: Dangling modifier: 'As specialists in the technology of deciphering messages' should modify 'cryptologists', but the subject that follows is 'complex mathematical formulas', which are not specialists.

sentence_construction.question: Llamas paragraph (click-to-select). Llamas, the South American relative of the camel, make excellent [pets, they] are very friendly and are well-liked by both people and other animals. In various parts of the world, people have herded llamas in [flocks, for they] are social animals that prefer to live in large packs. In South America, llamas helped the Andean civilization thrive in the high [mountains; their] high thirst tolerance, physical stamina, and ability to survive on a wide variety of plants make llamas important transport animals. Besides providing [transportation, llamas] offer wool, meat, and tallow for candles. Which part of the paragraph contains an error in sentence structure?
sentence_construction.reasoning: 'Llamas...make excellent pets' and 'they are very friendly...' are both independent clauses joined only by a comma - a comma splice. The other three options are all correctly punctuated (comma+coordinating conjunction 'for', semicolon joining independent clauses, comma after introductory phrase).

sentence_construction.question: The successful fundraising campaign for the school's field trip continued for a week teachers counted the money every morning with growing amazement. Which edit should be made to correct the sentence?
sentence_construction.reasoning: Run-on: 'continued for a week' and 'teachers counted the money...' are both independent clauses with no punctuation joining them; a semicolon fixes it (a comma alone would create a splice).

sentence_construction.question: Winter weather provides us with the opportunity to do so many outdoor activities, we can ski down mountains, skate on ice, make snowmen, and glide downhill on a snowboard. Which revision corrects the error in sentence structure in the sentence?
sentence_construction.reasoning: Comma splice: 'outdoor activities' and 'we can ski down mountains...' are both independent clauses joined only by a comma; a semicolon fixes it. B, C, D would incorrectly break up the comma-separated list.

sentence_construction.question: The electric fan was an ingenious invention for keeping people cool during the summer it was popular only briefly, however, until the air conditioner was invented. Which edit should be made to correct the sentence?
sentence_construction.reasoning: Run-on: 'during the summer' and 'it was popular only briefly...' are both independent clauses with no punctuation joining them.

sentence_construction.question: Russian language paragraph (click-to-select). Even though its structure and alphabet are not similar to those of Romance [languages, Russian] has many parallels [to French the] Russian alphabet has used various versions of Cyrillic script since about the tenth century. Cyrillic is a modified Greek [alphabet, which] has a few letters resembling those in the Latin [alphabet. Approximately] 300 million people throughout the world speak Russian. Which part of the paragraph contains an error in sentence structure?
sentence_construction.reasoning: Run-on: there is no punctuation between 'parallels to French' and 'The Russian alphabet has used...', which starts a new independent clause - needs a period or semicolon.

sentence_construction.question: Archerfish passage, sentence 5: 'Archerfish are generally small, from five to ten centimeters, they are capable of growing as large as 40 centimeters.' How should sentence 5 be revised?

options.A: Archerfish are generally small, from five to ten centimeters, they is capable of growing as large as 40 centimeters.
options.B: Archerfish are generally tiny, from five to ten centimeters, they are capable of growing as large as 40 centimeters.
options.C: Archerfish are generally small, from five to ten centimeters, but they are capable of growing as large as 40 centimeters.
options.D: Fish are generally small, from five to ten centimeters, they are capable of growing as large as 40 centimeters.

sentence_construction.reasoning: Comma splice between two independent clauses; adding 'but' fixes it and correctly signals the logical contrast (small on average, but capable of growing much larger).

sentence_construction.question: Shakespeare paragraph. (1) Despite borrowing many of his plots from history and myths, with other playwrights providing him with some of his dialogue, William Shakespeare is considered one of the most original writers of all time. (2) In addition to writing sonnets and poems, Shakespeare wrote 37 plays, including Hamlet and Macbeth. (3) Interestingly, Shakespeare originally did not intend to publish his works. (4) Due to inconsistent records over the centuries, some of his plays have developed several variations, the original sources of which experts still do not agree on. Which sentence contains an error in its construction and should be revised?
sentence_construction.ambiguous_note: No sentence has a clear, confident grammatical error on close analysis - all four are structurally sound, though sentence 1 stacks two long introductory modifying phrases which makes it complex/hard to parse. Flagging as uncertain rather than forcing a guess.

punctuation.question: Read this sentence. White roses represent unity, yellow roses show friendship, and red roses signify love however, many people believe red roses are the most cherished within the genus Rosa. Which edit should be made to correct the sentence?
punctuation.reasoning: Two independent clauses joined by conjunctive adverb 'however' need a semicolon before it: '...signify love; however, many people believe...'

punctuation.question: Read this sentence. In constant demand as a piano teacher my brother David has never been busier than he is now. How should the sentence be revised?
punctuation.reasoning: Introductory descriptive phrase 'In constant demand as a piano teacher' must be set off by a comma before the subject 'my brother David' begins.

punctuation.question: Unable to decide between a career in law and one in medicine Jemma combined her two interests and studied forensic medicine. Which edit should be made to correct the sentence?
punctuation.reasoning: The introductory phrase 'Unable to decide between a career in law and one in medicine' must be set off by a comma before the main clause 'Jemma combined...' begins.

punctuation.question: Bicycling paragraph (drag format). (1) Bicycling is a mainstream form of transportation in Japanese cities. (2) Nearly every type of person uses a bicycle blue-collar workers, office workers in suits, parents toting babies, and students. (3) In the United States, however, bicycling is more often seen as a recreational activity or form of exercise than as a means of transportation. (4) An exception is that American children often rely on bikes because they have fewer transportation options. Which sentence in the paragraph contains an error in construction?
punctuation.reasoning: Sentence 2 needs a colon after 'bicycle' to introduce the list that follows (blue-collar workers, office workers, parents, students) - without it, the sentence runs together confusingly.

punctuation.question: The newly constructed athletic complex features a myriad of amenities multipurpose gymnasiums, an elevated jogging track, squash courts, and exercise studios. Which edit should be made to correct the sentence?
punctuation.reasoning: A colon is needed after 'amenities' to introduce the list of amenities that follows.

punctuation.question: Violet Palmer-professional basketball referee and one of the first women to officiate a National Basketball Association (NBA) game started her journey to forging her name in basketball's history in a typical way: she played the sport. Which edit should be made to correct the sentence?
punctuation.reasoning: The appositive describing Violet Palmer opens with a dash and must close with a second dash right before the main verb 'started'; without it, 'game started her journey' misleadingly reads as if 'game' is the subject.

punctuation.question: The summer intern job description listed a number of requirements including interest in community development, strong communication skills, and familiarity with social networking sites. Which edit should be made to correct the sentence?
punctuation.reasoning: A comma is needed before 'including' to set off the nonessential list that explains the requirements.

punctuation.question: One of the most notorious pieces in the Yale University Library is the Vinland Map; though valued at $1 million when donated in the 1950s the map's authenticity has been hotly debated for years. Which edit should be made to correct the sentence?
punctuation.reasoning: The introductory concessive clause 'though valued at $1 million when donated in the 1950s' must be followed by a comma before the main clause 'the map's authenticity has been hotly debated' begins.

punctuation.question: Diamond-one of the hardest substances on Earth as well as a tremendous heat insulator would be an ideal material for countless industrial and commercial uses were it not for its immense cost. Which edit should be made to correct the sentence?
punctuation.reasoning: The opening dash before 'one of the hardest substances...' must be closed with a second dash right before the main clause 'would be an ideal material' begins.

punctuation.question: Inca paragraph (underlined-phrase format). The Inca ruled a well-developed empire in South America... For example, this highly advanced culture had carefully designed suspension bridges which linked the network of roads. In addition, locations like Machu Picchu had impressive architecture... To maintain their agriculture, the Inca used irrigation systems and terraces along the hillsides. Which revision corrects the error in sentence structure in the paragraph?
punctuation.reasoning: 'suspension bridges which linked the network of roads' is a nonrestrictive clause (extra descriptive info, not identifying a specific subset of bridges) and needs a comma before 'which'.

punctuation.question: Samuel Barber paragraph (click-to-select format). Samuel Barber composed numerous symphonies, operas, and quartets, all of which express personal emotion. Encouraged by his musical family, he took piano and vocal lessons and began composing the first piece of his musical career at age seven. Although the orchestral arrangement is more famous Samuel Barber's Adagio was originally written for string quartet. For an American, Barber had impressive command of operatic tradition, which helped him earn two Pulitzer Prizes. Which revision corrects the error in sentence structure in the paragraph?
punctuation.reasoning: The introductory concessive clause 'Although the orchestral arrangement is more famous' needs a comma before the main clause 'Samuel Barber's Adagio was originally written...' begins.

punctuation.question: Bicycle technology paragraph. (1) Technology has greatly improved bicycles over the years; in 1868, the first known bike race featured bicycles that each weighed 160 pounds. (2) Today, racing bicycles weigh under 20 pounds. (3) These lighter bikes, often without brakes and gears are used by professional cyclists for time trials. (4) These bicycles also have specialized racing tires with an inner tube made of thin rubber and an outer tire cover made of cotton or silk. Which sentence contains an error in its construction and should be revised?
